title: Abolishing the U.S. Electoral College for Direct Popular Vote
rootClaim: The United States Electoral College should be abolished via constitutional amendment in favor of a direct national popular vote system.

branches.text: Democratic Equality & One-Person-One-Vote Principle: The Electoral College fundamentally violates democratic fairness by weighting individual votes unequally based on geographic state residency.

children.text: Anti-Majoritarian Mandate Crisis: Allowing a candidate to win the executive office while losing the national popular vote undermines democratic mandate and public trust in governing institutions.
Constitutional Republic Intent: The United States is structured as a constitutional federal republic of states rather than a pure majoritarian democracy, safeguarding smaller states from domination.
Modern Elector Reality: Electorate voting has evolved into individual citizen participation; state-level winner-take-all rules distort popular intent without fulfilling original framer Intent.
Battleground State Geographic Distortion: Campaigns ignore majority safe states, focusing policy promises, campaign spending, and voter turnout efforts exclusively on a few swing states.

Broad Coalition Incentivization: Electoral College rules force candidates to construct broad geographic coalitions across rural, suburban, and urban interests rather than appealing solely to dense population centers.

branches.text: Federalism Defense & Administrative Stability: The Electoral College protects federalism and isolates election recount disputes within specific state borders.

children.text: Recount Crisis Isolation: Under the Electoral College, close or disputed elections require localized state recounts rather than triggering a logistically impossible nationwide recount.

National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (NPVIC): States can coordinate through interstate compacts to ensure winner of national popular vote wins electoral votes, sidestepping constitutional gridlock.
Mitigation of Majoritarian Tyranny: Protecting lower-population states guarantees that regional interests retain constitutional leverage in national policy decisions.

definitions.description: The official constitutional body of electors chosen by individual states to cast votes for the President and Vice President of the United States.
An agreement among U.S. states and D.C. to award all their electoral votes to whichever presidential candidate wins the overall popular vote nationwide.
A political scenario wherein a democratic majority pursues exclusively its own interests at the severe expense of minority groups or regions.
A system of government in which power is divided between a central national government and constituent state governments.
